reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a walkthrough of a random video-chat application, including account setup, gender and region selection, and swipe-based matching. Its promotion concerns free video calling over Wi-Fi, and the request to follow the channel is ordinary audience engagement rather than a linked payment, investment, credential request, or deceptive offer. The visible setup fields and live conversations are not described as involving misuse or a deceptive mechanism.

This is a FREE video chat to girls app all over the world.

opening.argument: Judge the offer as a sequence, not just a tutorial: viewers are promised free access to video chats with girls worldwide, then shown how to install the app and sign up. The description also qualifies that promise by saying not all countries remain freely enabled. That qualification matters because the attractive offer comes first, while its limitation is easy to miss. The demonstrated action is therefore tied to a benefit the video itself acknowledges may not be available as advertised.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The walkthrough does show gender selection, region selection and swiping. Those steps do not establish that the advertised free worldwide access is available after installation. The defense treats the qualification as harmless, but the description expressly says some countries are no longer freely enabled. Showing how the interface works answers a different question from whether the offer inducing viewers to try it holds up.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The limitation is disclosed in the same description as the free-access claim, not concealed behind a later action. The demonstration also describes a free global region option. Neither quote shows that viewers must pay, provide credentials to the presenter, or complete a separate claim flow to receive the advertised service. A qualified description of an app's availability is not, by itself, evidence of a deceptive offer.

opening.argument: Several signals deserve scrutiny together. The description repeats that the app is free, says there are no phone-call charges, and supplies an external article link; the title foregrounds live chats with girls. Yet the description concedes that free availability varies by country. A judge need not assume the link is malicious to see the concern: an emphatic, low-friction promise can move viewers toward an outside page and app before they give the limitation its proper weight.
